To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CMIP5 models have improved in their ability to simulate the global water cycle compared to CMIP3.

the water cycle of climate models is biased in a few models, that this bias is persistent over time in the control runs and hence should be taken in consideration, and that this bias can be detected with the closure of the moisture budget.

the multi-model mean of the global atmospheric moisture budget is consistent with the observed one, but that a few outlier models, that exhibit significant and changing biases in the control simulations, can distort the multi-model mean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a) the water cycle in the climate system and b) the evaluation of climate models with respect to their ability to reproduce this water cycle.
the evaluation of water cycle changes and their uncertainties in global and regional climate models.
the evaluation of the global water balance in climate model control simulations and the identification of biases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMIP3 models have a tendency to underestimate precipitation and to overestimate evaporation.
, although the multi-model means are generally consistent with observations, the individual models are not.
the climate system is not in a steady state and that the models are still not able to reproduce the global hydrological cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

climate models can be considered to be consistent with each other and with observations, but they can also exhibit significant biases that need to be corrected in order to be used in climate predictions.
the water cycle is a good climate change indicator, as it is sensitive to climate change and is a robust indicator of climate change.

the water cycle in CMIPS5 climate models is in better shape than in CMIP3, but there are still significant biases that should be taken in consideration when using the models for climate change projections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CMIP5 models show a much better consistency among themselves than CMIP3 models.
climate models should not only be tested with respect to the observed climate but also with respect to each other.
climate model biases can be large and persistent over time, and that they can be used to improve climate predictions.
